profile.reading:
This is Equinix's GN1 facility at Via Lungobisagno Istria 14/A in Genoa, Italy, which Equinix's own dedicated facility page markets as Genoa's first world-class, carrier-neutral data center. Equinix states GN1 connects directly to its Milan ML5 facility, functioning together as a subsea cable hub for the Mediterranean region, reflecting Genoa's status as a major Italian port city where transcontinental submarine cables come ashore. Equinix's page gives the facility's colocation space as 560 square meters, or about 6,028 square feet, and states N+1 power redundancy, N+2 cooling redundancy, and a 99.9999%-plus global uptime guarantee, though it does not publish a specific IT capacity figure in megawatts or kilowatts. Equinix entered the European colocation market through its 2007 acquisition of IXEurope and expanded further through its 2015 acquisition of TelecityGroup, though Equinix's current GN1 page does not attribute the building to either predecessor company by name, so this registry does not assert a lineage. Equinix, founded in Silicon Valley in 1998 by former Digital Equipment Corporation facilities managers Al Avery and Jay Adelson, converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX; the company's own about page states a current global footprint of 281 data centers across six continents with more than 513,000 interconnections, while Wikipedia separately cites a close but not identical figure of approximately 260 data centers across 33 countries as of 2025, and this registry records both rather than reconciling them.

As an EU-based facility, this data center falls under the European Union's Energy Efficiency Directive reporting requirements, which since 2024 have required data centers above a minimum capacity threshold to report power usage effectiveness, water usage, and other sustainability metrics to a European Commission database, part of a broader EU push for standardized data center energy transparency that does not have a direct equivalent in most of the US markets covered elsewhere in this registry.
profile.facility_note: Equinix GN1, Genoa, Italy: marketed by Equinix as the city's first carrier-neutral data center and a Mediterranean subsea cable hub alongside Milan ML5.
